title: Nvidia Stock News (Oct 15, 2026): NVDA Falls 3.2% to $221.30
summary: Nvidia (NVDA) closed at $221.30 on October 14, 2026, down 3.16%, as chip stocks slid and the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.88%.
body_markdown:
## Why Nvidia Stock Fell


None of the sources reviewed named a company-specific cause for Wednesday's decline, so the move is best read against the wider selling in semiconductors, where several peers lost more than Nvidia did.


Two Nvidia-related stories ran around the session. According to[MT Newswires](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/nvidia-ceo-says-cut-off-235015911.html) , citing a Bloomberg interview published Wednesday, CEO Jensen Huang said Nvidia would consider halting chip supplies to customers developing unsafe AI, after first raising concerns with them.


Huang also said demand for AI infrastructure will keep exceeding component supply for years, and Nvidia is donating $250 million over five years to UK AI safety research. The report did not link these remarks to the share move.


Separately, as reported by[Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/microsoft-just-unveiled-brand-ai-211706659.html) ,[Microsoft (MSFT)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/msft/) unveiled its Maia 300 AI chip on Monday. Microsoft says the chip processes 40% more tokens per megawatt than GPUs, with production starting in 2027. Microsoft shares fell 1.80% on Wednesday.


## NVDA Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Huang said demand for AI infrastructure will keep running ahead of component supply for years, per MT Newswires.
- Motley Fool notes Nvidia remains part of Microsoft's AI mix and argues the Maia 300 competes on cost rather than raw power, with production not due until 2027.
- Trading volume ran 7.60% above average, and the stock remains 34.72% above its 52-week low.


### Risks


- Custom chips such as Microsoft's Maia 300 could handle lower-difficulty in-house AI workloads more cheaply, which Motley Fool says could weigh on Nvidia's sales volume even if its chips stay the most powerful.
- The stock fell more than the Nasdaq Composite on Wednesday, showing its exposure to broad selling in technology and chip stocks.
- Nvidia now trades 9.07% below its 52-week high of $243.37.
